body.statement: From \(Q=n^2 2^{n-1}\) nontrivial oracle answers, \(\operatorname{Alg}_E\) returns \((G^\star,\operatorname{Comp}(G))\) over the full candidate universe \(U_{\to}\cup U_{\leftrightarrow}\); for every directed edge, bidirected edge, directed loop, or bidirected loop \(e\in E(G^\star)\), \(e\in\operatorname{Comp}(G)\) iff \(\Sigma_E(G^\star-e)\neq\Sigma_E(G^\star)\).
body.justification: It converts existence into exact structure identification.
body.gap: Greatest-plus-compelled recovery exists for \(\mu\), not mixed E-separation.
body.consumer: Discovery reports compelled, optional, and impossible process mechanisms.

obligation.what_is_open: Show that the componentwise union enumerated from the singleton oracle is itself E-equivalent to the unknown graph over the unrestricted finite-DMG class.
obligation.obstruction: Enumeration and the compelled-edge deletion criterion are finite and explicit, but identifying the enumerated union with an in-class greatest representative is exactly unrestricted union closure.
obligation.attempted: The singleton table was shown to determine the full E-model, and both the union and intersection of all matching finite graphs are computable.  The deletion-test equivalence follows conditionally from a greatest member and antitonicity.  No independent route around union closure was found.
obligation.partial_result:
Singleton composition proves that the \(Q=n^2 2^{n-1}\) queried entries with \(C\subseteq V\setminus\{a\}\) determine the complete E-model, since every omitted singleton query has its source \(a_0\) conditioned and is therefore separated.  Finite enumeration consequently recovers the componentwise union of all matching graphs and their edge intersection.  If unrestricted union closure holds, that union is \(G^\star\); moreover, for \(e\in E(G^\star)\),
\[
 e\in\operatorname{Comp}(G)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Sigma_E(G^\star-e)\ne\Sigma_E(G^\star).
\]
Indeed, equality on the right supplies an equivalent graph omitting \(e\); conversely, if an equivalent \(K\) omits \(e\), then \(K\subseteq G^\star-e\subseteq G^\star\), and antitonicity gives signature equality.  Thus the algorithmic and deletion-test arguments are complete conditional reductions; only the assertion that the enumerated union remains E-equivalent is open.
